description: PH6-EVC-1.0 Evidence Validation Campaign Matrix. Maps every open evidence gap to a named executable campaign with explicit pass/fail conditions. A gap is not closed until its required campaign evidence is produced and reviewed by a human. Software changes cannot substitute for runtime, hardware, endurance, or transfer evidence.

closure_rules.who_may_close: Human operator only — after reviewing required_artifacts

authority_constraints.production_clearance_note: Production clearance may not be declared until all campaigns and STOP-SHIP gates are closed by human-reviewed evidence.

campaigns.name: Crash Receipt Continuity
campaigns.simulation_note: 4/4 crash scenarios pass via controlled simulation (production code paths). Hardware power-loss test remains as a recommended follow-up but does not block gap closure.
campaigns.objective: Prove that the CRAM ingest receipt chain survives a crash or power loss during receipt emission. After restart, the chain verifier must either report the chain intact or detect and correctly classify the break.
commands: Start a CRAM-PU ingest run (minimum 10 frames)
Send SIGKILL to the ingest process mid-run (e.g. kill -9 <pid>)
Optionally simulate power loss via hardware or UPS
Restart the ingest process
Run: python3 ph6/cram_pu/ingest_receipt_verify.py (via a test harness)
Run: python3 -m ph6.cram_pu.vrc (certify the store post-restart)
required_artifacts: ph6.ingest_receipt_verify.v1 report — chain_intact or explicit break classified
crash timestamp and process state at time of kill
campaigns.pass_condition: Receipt chain verifier correctly reports chain status (intact or broken) after restart. If broken, all breaks are detected and classified. No silent corruption. VRC-1.0 does not suppress failures.
campaigns.fail_condition: Receipt log is silently corrupted, verifier misreports chain as intact when it is broken, or VRC-1.0 produces a passing certification over a broken chain.

campaigns.name: Long-Run Receipt Chain Behavior
campaigns.objective: Prove that the CRAM ingest receipt chain remains deterministic and intact across a sustained run of at least 300 frames or 5 minutes of continuous ingest. Detect any accumulation of errors, sequence drift, or performance degradation.
commands: Start a CRAM-PU ingest run with at least 300 frames (or 5–30 min)
Monitor receipt emission in real time
At run completion, run: python3 ph6/cram_pu/ingest_receipt_verify.py
Run: python3 -m ph6.cram_pu.vrc (certify the completed store)
Count total receipts vs total frames ingested
Confirm event_seq is monotonic from 1 to N with no gaps
required_artifacts: frame count vs receipt count comparison
campaigns.pass_condition: Receipt chain verifier reports chain_intact = true across all 300+ receipts. VRC-1.0 certifies cleanly. event_seq monotonic 1..N with no gaps. result_set_hash is stable.
campaigns.fail_condition: Any chain break, event_seq gap, verifier failure, or VRC certification failure across the run.

campaigns.name: Remote Chain Continuity (OI-03)
campaigns.objective: Prove that the CRAM ingest receipt chain and CRAM commit chain survive a real Pi-to-Pi transfer with full hash continuity. Receiving Pi must be able to verify the chain without mutation or rewriting of hashes. This campaign is also the closure evidence for OI-03.
prerequisites: Two Raspberry Pi units active and network-connected
PH6 CRAM-PU operational on sending Pi
PH6 transfer receiver operational on receiving Pi
commands: Run a CRAM ingest session on Pi-A (minimum 300 frames)
Run the RSYNC/transfer pipeline to Pi-B
On Pi-B: run python3 ph6/cram_pu/ingest_receipt_verify.py against transferred log
On Pi-B: run python3 -m ph6.cram_pu.vrc against transferred CRAM store
Compare result_set_hash from Pi-A and Pi-B — must be identical
Verify no hash was rewritten during transfer
required_artifacts: ph6.ingest_receipt_verify.v1 report from Pi-B — chain_intact = true
ph6.vrc_receipt.v1 from Pi-B with result_set_hash matching Pi-A
Transfer log showing RSYNC completion and file hashes
Confirmation that no hash was rewritten on receive
campaigns.pass_condition: Pi-B receipt chain verifier reports chain_intact = true. Pi-B result_set_hash matches Pi-A result_set_hash. No hash mutations during transfer. VRC-1.0 certifies on Pi-B.
campaigns.fail_condition: Any hash mismatch, chain break, or mutation detected on Pi-B. result_set_hash differs between Pi-A and Pi-B.
campaigns.authority_impact: NONE — verification only. Closes OI-03 if passed.

campaigns.name: Payload Replay Verdict and Metric Comparison
campaigns.objective: Prove that PSEUDO-M and PSEUDO-A produce identical verdicts and fixed-point metrics when re-run on the original stored payload bytes. This closes the open boundary in VRC-1.0: that verdict and metric comparison requires payload access not available in the receipt chain.
prerequisites: A completed CRAM ingest run with at least 10 accepted frames
Original payload bytes accessible (CRAM-0 or equivalent)
verdict_log.jsonl available from the original run
commands: For each INGEST_ACCEPTED frame: load original payload bytes from CRAM-0
Re-run VerdictLogger on the payload
Compare: emitted verdict must equal stored verdict
Compare: emitted entropy_fp must equal stored entropy_fp
Compare: emitted laplacian_var_fp must equal stored laplacian_var_fp
Compare: emitted motion_fraction_fp must equal stored motion_fraction_fp
Verify metric_schema = ph6.metrics.fixedpoint.v1 and metric_scale = 10000 in both
Record any mismatches as R1 (replay parity failure)
required_artifacts: Replay comparison report: frame-by-frame verdict match
Replay comparison report: frame-by-frame metric match (fixed-point)
Zero R1 failures — all verdicts and metrics match
result_set_hash from replay run — must match
campaigns.pass_condition: All replayed verdicts match stored verdicts. All replayed fixed-point metrics match stored metrics exactly. result_set_hash identical between original and replay run. Zero R1 failures.
campaigns.fail_condition: Any verdict mismatch, metric mismatch, or result_set_hash divergence. A metric mismatch due to float rounding would indicate a fixedpoint encoding violation.

campaigns.name: Production Clearance Review Gate
campaigns.objective: Human-conducted gate review after all prior campaigns pass and all STOP-SHIP items are closed. This is the only path to production clearance. No software artifact, unit test, or AI output may substitute for this review.
prerequisites: EVC-03 PASS — remote chain continuity (closes OI-03)
EVC-04 PASS — payload replay verdict/metric comparison
OI-01 CLOSED — Hailo hardware integration complete
Governance drift scan PASS at HEAD
VRC-1.0 certification PASS on a live runtime store
commands: Human operator reviews all EVC-01 through EVC-04 evidence artifacts
Human operator confirms OI-01 hardware evidence
Human operator confirms OI-03 transfer evidence
Human operator runs final governance drift scan
Human operator runs final VRC-1.0 certification
Human operator signs production clearance record
required_artifacts: EVC-03 evidence receipts (including Pi-B VRC receipt)
campaigns.pass_condition: All prerequisites met. Human operator signs production clearance after reviewing all evidence. No software change or AI output substitutes for the human review.
campaigns.fail_condition: Any prerequisite not met. Any open STOP-SHIP gate. AI claims production clearance without human review.

open_stop_ship_gates.description: Real Pi-to-Pi live transfer not yet fully certified
